Title: Awareness is required regarding early recognition and treatment for heart valve disorders
NewsSummary: "Conditions relating to the heart are the leading cause of death in the world. In a developing country like Pakistan, both coronary artery disease and valvular heart diseases are prevalent," said Dr Hasanat Sharif, Consultant Cardiothoracic Surgeon

content.text: "Conditions relating to the heart are the leading cause of death in the world. In a developing country like Pakistan, both coronary artery disease and valvular heart diseases are prevalent," said Dr Hasanat Sharif, Consultant Cardiothoracic Surgeon at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving the presentation on "Diagnosis and treatment of Heart Valve Disorder" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' a monthly health awareness programme held on December 23, 2000.

Dr Hasanat Sharif said, "Valular heart disorders can be congenital (present at birth) or maybe acquired later in life. Acquired valve diseases are those problems that develop with valves that were once normal. They may be either rheumatic or due to infection. Symptoms include a history of infection, rheumatic fever (following untreated sore throat), shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations or murmur detected by a physician."

Dr Hasanat Sharif explained, "Treatment options available are medicines, valvuloplasty, valvotomy, repair and replacement. Surgery is safe and effective if performed early, before the heart starts to fail. Risk to life with surgery is about three to five percent. The new valve is susceptible to infection; therefore antibiotics are given for dental and lower G1 procedures. There can be a risk of clot formation if the patient is not adequately anti-coagulated or a risk of bleeding, should a patient be over anti-coagulated. Recovery following surgery takes about five to seven days but convalescence continues for six to eight weeks."

Dr Sharif concluded by saying, "heart valve disorders are mostly preventable. Awareness is required regarding early recognition and treatment of conditions like rheumatic fever and systemic infections. It is important to realize that treatment is available. Early diagnosis leads to early treatment, which can be carried out at low risk to life.

The speaker and panelists, which included Dr Shahid Sami and Dr Saulat Hasnain Fatimi, Consultant cardiothoracic Surgeons at AKUH participated in the lively question and answered session at the end of the program.
